prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
Sorry to hear you were in an accident — that can be stressful. I can’t pick one single lawyer for you, but I can help you choose the right personal injury attorney in Pleasanton and offer to find local options if you’d like.

Quick legal deadlines (important)
- California personal injury statute of limitations: generally 2 years from the date of the injury to file a lawsuit.
- Property-damage claims: generally 3 years.
- Claims against a government entity: much shorter — often 6 months to file an administrative claim. If any defendant is a public agency, act quickly.

How to choose the right lawyer
Look for an attorney who:
- Focuses on car-accident / personal-injury cases (not a generalist).
- Has substantial experience handling cases like yours (similar injury severity, liability issues).
- Has trial experience and a record of settlements/verdicts (you want someone who will take the case to court if needed).
- Works on contingency (most PI lawyers do — they only get paid if you recover).
- Communicates clearly and is responsive (who will be your point person?).
- Knows how to handle medical liens, health insurance and subrogation issues.
- Has good client reviews and a clean record with the State Bar of California.

Questions to ask in the initial consultation (most are free)
- What percent of your practice is car-accident/personal injury?
- How many cases like mine have you handled? Any sample settlements/verdicts?
- Do you try cases or do you usually settle? What’s your trial experience?
- How do your fees and costs work? (Typical: contingency fee — e.g., ~33% if settled before suit, higher if suit/filed; costs are usually advanced and reimbursed from recovery.)
- Who will handle my case day-to-day?
- How will you handle medical bills, liens, and communications with my health insurer?
- What’s a realistic timeline and likely value range for my case?
- Can you give references from recent clients?

Documents to bring to a consult
- Police report / incident number.
- Photos or video of the accident scene, vehicles, and injuries.
- Medical treatment records and bills, recent doctor notes.
- Pay stubs showing lost wages.
- Insurance correspondence (your insurer and other parties).
- Witness names/contact info, if available.

Red flags to watch for
- Promises of a specific dollar amount up front.
- Pushy “sign now” tactics without reviewing your records.
- Unclear fee agreement or no written contract.
- Poor communication during the intake process.

Local resources and how I can help
- Check attorney credentials and discipline history at the State Bar of California (calbar.ca.gov).
- Use local reviews (Google, Avvo, Martindale) and the Alameda County Bar Association referral service for vetted attorneys.
- If you’d like, I can search for and provide a short list (3–5) of personal injury attorneys in Pleasanton or the Tri-Valley area with contact info and a short summary of each. Tell me: (a) the ZIP code you’re in or how far you’re willing to travel, (b) a short description of your injuries and whether a government entity is involved, and (c) whether you prefer large firms or local/smaller boutiques.

Immediate steps you should take now
- If you haven’t already, get medical attention and follow doctor orders.
- Preserve evidence (photos, damaged property, vehicle, messages).
- Don’t give recorded statements to the other party’s insurer without talking to a lawyer.
- Start saving medical bills and time-off-work documentation.

If you want, I can now compile a short list of Pleasanton/Tri-Valley personal injury lawyers for you to contact. Would you like that? If so, give me your ZIP code and a couple of details about the accident/injuries.
